Subject: Endpoint cutover — customer risk heatmap & comms play

Team — starting the thread to synthesize impact and finalize comms for next month’s endpoint/model cutover. High-level asks below; I’d like edits and ownerships by end of day tomorrow so we can publish the customer note on Thursday.

Quick context: We’re retiring the legacy embed endpoints and routing to the consolidated chat/generation endpoints. Expected start of enforced cutover: 2026-12-01. We already have a small set of customers who will need special runway/exemptions.

Asks:
- Ben: update the customer risk heatmap (attached) with migration effort estimate (low/med/high) and likely SLA exception requests.
- Marissa: call out any product gaps customers cite (e.g., missing variant parity, tokenization differences) and draft the short customer note (one-pager + migration checklist).
- Karthik: confirm fallback behavior and whether we can keep the legacy routing for a hard-exemption set for +30 days after cutover; include perf/cost delta.
- Laura: confirm CS comms cadence and whether we need AE/SE outreach for accounts in high-risk lane.

Please reply inline on the heatmap. I attached a first-pass sheet (customer-risk-heatmap.xlsx) with a couple of rows filled; it’s intentionally sparse. Copy any external owners (Tom/Shaun) after we agree on wording.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Redwood Inference

Filing product asks here — pulled from support threads and recent CSM notes:

- Variant parity: Four accounts explicitly rely on legacy "embed-v0" behavior; for two of these we can map to the new "embed-compat" variant but need to add a short migration note re: vector normalization differences.
- Tokenization: Two accounts report token accounting differences in aggregated billing exports; engineering can add a compatibility flag in exports, but that’s a small follow-up (2–3 sprint story).
- Exemptions: propose we offer a 30-day soft exemption (no enforcement) and a managed migration lane (SE + dev hours) for accounts marked high. Any exemption beyond 30 days requires Director sign-off and a basic SOW.

I drafted a short customer note (draft-customer-note.md) — it’s rough but covers the What/When/How and links to the migration checklist. Please review and add bullet points for any account-specific items.

Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Endpoint cutover — customer risk heatmap & comms play

Technical note / constraints:

- We can implement a routing shim to keep legacy endpoints alive for a whitelist of customers for +30 days with minimal risk; cost delta will be ~6–9% on affected capacity due to extra routing and KV cache duplication.
- A longer exemption (+60–90 days) is technically possible but increases operational overhead and testing matrix for our rollout. I recommend limiting long exemptions to verified enterprise SOWs only.
- Fallback behavior: requests to legacy endpoints should auto-redirect with a 307 and a clear response body explaining the migration path. For managed migrations we can offer a migration token that preserves parity for rate-limited endpoints.

If we want to instrument regressions for tokenization differences, add an opt-in flag that records token deltas for 2 weeks post-cutover (low perf impact).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

- Approve the proposed 30-day soft exemption window plus a managed migration lane for accounts flagged "high" in Ben’s heatmap. Any extension >30 days requires Director-level approval and a short SOW.
- Marissa: please finalize the customer note; we will publish the public notice on 2026-11-11 and send targeted emails to high/medium accounts on 2026-11-12.
- Ben: schedule SE outreach for Acme (Tom Greer) and block a migration workshop week-of-11/22. Please include the runbook and SOW template in the invite.
- Karthik: implement the routing shim with 307 behavior and add the opt-in token-delta flag; target merge by 2026-11-20.
- Hannah: I’ll coordinate with Legal on a brief SLO addendum and with Revenue for notification to AEs.

I’ll run a short cross-functional review on Thursday 11/11 at 10am PT — calendar invite coming.

Laura Bennett
